items.rationale: Section 2.6.4 excludes glazing from accidental damage cover. No optional glazing cover is shown, so §3.5(a) excludes the replacement.
Drilling to receive the replacement pane or its hardware is preparatory glazing work under §1.3 and is excluded by §3.5(b).
Fitting the replacement pane is glazing work excluded by §3.5(b); under §7.1.11 it does not become payable because the same incident damaged the side table.

Section 3.5(b) excludes disposal of the broken pane, and §5.2.1 does not cover debris from an item whose damage is uninsured. The conditional estimate uses the €30–34 glass-disposal benchmark in Case 8.

items.description: Repair of dented solid-wood side table
items.rationale: The sudden impact damaged insured household contents under §§2.6.1 and 4.2.6. Sections 7.1.1(b) and 7.1.5 allow local dent repair and finish restoration, estimated at €280 gross with no stated deductible.
Sections 3.6(a) and 7.1.9 exclude the old scratches on the second cabinet, even though the touch-up was billed with the covered repair.
Under §7.1.12, the contractor's first attendance is payable in full if the covered table repair was carried out at that visit. The old-scratch work does not reduce the reasonable €25 gross charge.
Section 7.1.12 excludes a return visit by the same contractor unless the insurer agreed to it in advance; no approval is indicated.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes separate administrative flat rates as business overhead rather than repair costs.
